overview.text: Theophany depicts Christ’s baptism by John in the Jordan and the manifestation of the Trinity. Hopko distinguishes the feast’s present focus from the earlier broader Epiphany celebration, which also included events surrounding Christ’s birth. Its printed date is January 6.

blocks.text: Christ stands in the Jordan, John extends his hand toward him, and angels wait opposite. A descending ray and dove indicate the divine manifestation.

blocks.text: Hopko explains Epiphany as manifestation or shining forth. In the Gospel event, the Father bears witness to the Son and the Holy Spirit appears as a dove. John’s baptism therefore reveals Christ as Messiah and as one of the Holy Trinity. The source links the feast with its biblical readings and the Great Blessing of Water, interpreting Christ’s immersion in relation to the sanctification of creation.
